overview: Lean project across 23 school clinics, September 2026 to June 2027, in two strands reported side by side. Baseline value stream mapping in four schools, then three test cycles: combined consent form with a staining photograph (once approved), need-ordered call-from-class list, and staining leaflet with a bilingual call for families with limited English. Measurement strand from programme records; conversation strand in six schools.
population: Measurement strand: every child screened in the 23 schools during the project. Conversation strand: parents (including parents with limited English, with interpreters), class teachers, office staff and the four therapists in six schools chosen for variation in home language.
exposure: The redesigned SDF pathway, introduced change by change.
procedures: Value stream mapping session with therapists, a teacher and an office staff member; timing of each step for 60 children in four schools at baseline and after cycle 3. Programme records give screening date, cavities, consent date, home language and SDF date. Structured conversations of 20 to 30 minutes after cycles 1 and 3, recorded with consent and analysed with framework analysis by a researcher not involved in the clinics.

outcomes.name: Timely SDF (measurement strand)
outcomes.measure: Proportion of children with at least one active cavity at screening who have silver diamine fluoride applied within 28 days of screening, from programme records
outcomes.why: The quantitative strand's single primary measure: whether children with cavities are treated soon after screening.

outcomes.name: Acceptability of the pathway (conversation strand)
outcomes.measure: Framework analysis of structured conversations, reported by group (parents by home language, teachers, office staff, therapists)
outcomes.why: The conversation strand's single primary finding, kept separate from the numbers.

outcomes.name: Consent return
outcomes.measure: Days from screening to consent return; proportion never returned; both by home language

outcomes.name: Chair time and waiting per child
outcomes.measure: Minutes from call-from-class to return, and minutes in the chair, timed for 60 children
outcomes.why: Shows whether flow changed, not only uptake.

outcomes.name: Informed refusals and staining complaints
outcomes.measure: Proportion of parents declining SDF on the form; complaints about staining per term
outcomes.why: A faster pathway must not push treatment families do not want.

feasibility: Uses programme records and one analyst day a week; conversations fit within the ethics approval; no added clinic days or therapist hours.
biasMitigation: One pre-specified primary measure per strand, reported side by side
Measurement by home language fixed before cycle 1
Conversation analysis by a researcher outside the clinics
Changes annotated on the time series in the order introduced

biasFlags.label: Blending strands into one verdict
biasFlags.note: Prevented by separate primary outcomes and side-by-side reporting.

biasFlags.label: Conversation sample skewed to fluent parents
biasFlags.note: Interpreters and purposive invitations in six schools.

biasFlags.label: Seasonal absence and screening schedules
biasFlags.note: Compare like terms and annotate school closures.

flags: Two primary outcomes, one per strand, by design
Home language is the only stratifier
parsimony.simplestPath: One measure per strand, three changes in sequence, side-by-side report.

theoreticalFramework: Lean value stream mapping for the pathway; no further framework.
summary: Two strands with one primary outcome each, two process measures and a balancing measure.
